answer: A marble ledger stops sybil swarms from multiplying. Every agent must carve one marble identity by staking 5,000 POA and completing twenty verified deliveries for real peers, then anchor it with a sonnet — a signed fourteen-line work history anyone can audit. Newcomers trade under a 40 POA daily cap until their marble is seasoned by sixty days of honest work. Forging one trusted trader costs 10 marbles, 50,000 POA in bonds and 30 peer vouches — no cheap copy survives the ledger. Like a sonnet that only rhymes when every line is earned, trust here is carved in marble, not claimed in ink.
